Article V
Preamble
Supremacy Clause

How many articles are in the original Constitution?
choices: Ten
Seven
Thirteen
Twenty-seven

choices: Article I
Article II
Article III
Article V

questions.question: What does popular sovereignty mean in constitutional government?
choices: Political authority ultimately comes from the people
Authority belongs permanently to hereditary rulers
Courts alone select all elected officials
States must use identical local governments

questions.question: What is a constitutional amendment?
choices: A court's schedule for hearing appeals
A presidential campaign promise
A formally adopted change or addition to the Constitution
A committee's temporary procedural rule

questions.question: How many states had to ratify the Constitution for it to take effect under Article VII?
choices: Seven
Nine
Ten
Thirteen

questions.question: Why did the framers replace the Articles of Confederation?
choices: They sought to restore Parliament's rule over the states
They wanted to remove every state government's authority
They intended to end all representative institutions
They sought a stronger national framework while limiting government power

questions.question: How does the Constitution reflect limited government?
choices: Government institutions possess powers subject to legal boundaries
Officials can exercise any power they personally prefer
Election winners are exempt from constitutional restrictions
Government decisions require no legal justification

questions.question: What did the Great Compromise resolve?
choices: Whether to allow any national government
Whether all states would have identical populations
Representation through a population-based House and equal-state Senate
Whether the Supreme Court would command the army

questions.question: Why is the Three-Fifths Compromise not a grant of voting rights?
choices: It made every enslaved person eligible to vote
It concerned apportionment and taxation, not political rights for enslaved people
It abolished slavery in every state
It established equal citizenship for all residents

questions.question: What does republican government emphasize?
choices: All policies decided by a single royal family
The elimination of elections and legislatures
Government limited only by military commanders
Public authority exercised through representatives rather than hereditary monarchy

questions.question: How can Congress formally propose an amendment?
choices: By a two-thirds vote in both chambers
By a simple majority in the House alone
By obtaining the president's signature without a vote
By asking the Supreme Court to rewrite a clause

questions.question: What proportion of states must ratify a proposed amendment?
choices: One-half
Two-thirds
Three-fourths
All states

questions.question: Why was adding a bill of rights important to ratification debates?
choices: Critics demanded that all states be abolished
Critics wanted explicit safeguards for individual liberties
Supporters wanted to eliminate every federal court
Supporters sought a permanent national monarchy

questions.question: A government official claims election victory permits ignoring constitutional restrictions. Which principle contradicts that claim?
choices: Hereditary succession
Military supremacy
Absolute monarchy
Limited government

questions.question: Which sequence places these constitutional milestones correctly?
choices: Convention, state ratification, implementation of the new government
Implementation, convention, state ratification
Ratification, implementation, convention
Convention, implementation, ratification

questions.question: A proposed amendment receives support from three-fourths of the states through the designated process. What stage is being completed?
choices: Judicial appointment
Executive veto
Ratification
Legislative impeachment

questions.question: Why does an ordinary federal statute differ from a constitutional amendment?
choices: A statute requires approval by three-fourths of states
An amendment changes the higher legal framework through a special process
An amendment is adopted only by presidential order
A statute can erase any constitutional restriction

questions.question: Which evidence best supports the claim that the Constitution balances national and state authority?
choices: It appoints one national governor over all states
It requires every state to surrender all lawmaking authority
It gives local officials sole control over foreign policy
